_readme: Renames this SDK has performed, for the one case a jar diff cannot work out on its own.
== What an upgrade does, and why this file is so small ==
When Studio upgrades a bot it holds both jars and diffs them. A member the bot calls that the newer
jar does not offer is replaced with a DEFAULT VALUE of the type it used to return -- false, 0, "",
null, or the whole statement deleted when it returned void -- and the enclosing function is marked
@NeedsReview so the user is walked through every one of them afterwards. The repair's job is to make
the bot compile; the user's job is to make it correct.
That needs nothing declared anywhere, which is why the fix kinds, the arity scopes, the coverage rule
and the ordered replay that used to live in this file are all gone. Pointing one member at another is
guessing: two members need not share a return type, an arity or any semantics, and a repair that
guesses wrong produces a bot that compiles and behaves differently -- the one outcome worse than a
compile error.
== The exception: a rename is not a removal ==
Read as a removal, `ImageClicker` -> `IClicker` is hundreds of deleted statements across someone's
project. So the pairing has to be known, and there are two ways it can be:
1. @ApiId, and this is the one to use. A stable kebab-case id on the type (com.botmaker.sdk.api.ApiId,
CLASS retention, read straight out of the jar) that both releases spell the same way, so the diff
pairs them with nothing written down here. Rename the class freely; keep the id.
2. THIS FILE, for what the ids cannot reach: anything renamed relative to a release that predates
them (v1.0.26 carries none), and any pairing you want to state by hand.
An id pairs the TYPE NAME and nothing else -- every member is still checked one by one against the
newer type. So an id kept across a redesign degrades into "the type was renamed, and most of its
members had no counterpart": defaults and review marks, never a rewrite that is silently wrong. The
rule that keeps it honest: an id is RETIRED when its role disappears, never re-pointed at a different
class.
== The shape ==
"schema":   2, required. Studio refuses a file whose schema it does not know -- whole, and saying so
-- and still reports everything else, because that comes from diffing the jars and needs
no file at all.
"versions": { "<version>": [ { "from": ..., "to": ... } ] }, keyed by the release that DID the
rename. Both sides are written the same way:
a type   -> com.botmaker.sdk.api.vision.ImageClicker
a member -> com.botmaker.sdk.api.vision.ImageFinder#find
a ctor   -> com.botmaker.sdk.api.Point#<init>
a field  -> com.botmaker.sdk.api.interaction.Key#ENTER   (an enum constant IS a static
field, so it is spelled this way too)
== Why the version keys, when nothing replays any more ==
A bot can jump several releases at once. If 2.0.0 renamed foo -> bar and 3.0.0 renamed bar -> baz, a
bot on 1.x upgrading straight to 3.0.0 still spells it foo, and neither entry matches that on its own.
Studio walks the versions in (from, to] in ascending order and COMPOSES them into a single map
foo -> baz, then makes one pass. That is a map composition, not a re-run of passes: renames compose,
and composing is the only thing this file now describes.
'versions' is empty because nothing has been renamed yet. v1.0.26 is the last release predating all of
this, and it carries no @ApiId -- so the first rename after it is the one case that must be written
here rather than left to the ids.
